clue.text: Mad proposal for travel

parts.note: loco is slang for mad or crazy
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting for a vote

explanation.surface: Someone's crazy plan for getting about.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotion is movement from place to place, the act of getting about.

clue.text: Laid about the old queen

parts.note: slang: to have laid someone is to have 'done' them, so laid gives did
about can mean round, and a round thing is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone has been rough with an elderly monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The old queen is the legendary queen of Carthage who loved Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido is the legendary ancient ruler of Carthage, a queen of long ago.

clue.text: "Nor any of this to drink", each observed after demise of albatross

indicators.note: observed after means the next piece is seen following the previous one
the demise of a word is its end, so take the final letter of albatross

explanation.surface: After the albatross dies, everyone sees there is nothing fit to drink, as in Coleridge's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner: 'Water, water, every where, / Nor any drop to drink', written after the albatross is shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean is salt water that cannot be drunk, the becalmed mariner's torment.

clue.text: Ill-tempered Romeo gatecrashes this New Year

indicators.note: to gatecrash is to get in uninvited, so one letter forces its way inside the others
new signals that the letters of this are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grumpy Romeo crashes this year's New Year party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' makes SHIT from THIS; R gatecrashes it to give SHIRT, and Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirty is British slang for annoyed, cross or bad-tempered.

clue.text: The lingua franca of Wimbledon, say?

definitions.text: The lingua franca of Wimbledon, say?

parts.words: The lingua franca of Wimbledon, say?
parts.note: a lingua franca is shared speech; Wimbledon, home of the tennis, is also a London suburb with a famous stretch of public open land, so its speech is jokingly that land's tongue

explanation.surface: What tongue do they talk at the Wimbledon tennis championships?
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon Common is a large public park in south-west London; the pun reads its name as a description of shared speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A lingua franca is a shared tongue that speakers of different native tongues all use.

clue.text: Close to holding a third boozy anniversary

indicators.note: holding means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: by can mean close to, as in standing by the door

indicators.note: boozy suggests the letters of a third are drunkenly jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunken celebration nearly takes in a third anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozy' turns A THIRD into IRTHDA, which BY holds between its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday is the yearly return of the day someone was born.

clue.text: Make insensitive dean search for redemption

indicators.note: redemption suggests reform and change, so the letters are remade into something new

explanation.surface: A dean goes looking for salvation and grows callous instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for redemption' rearranges the letters of DEAN SEARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To case-harden is literally to toughen steel's surface, figuratively to make someone callous.

clue.text: Wherefrom the acts observed peeking into bedrooms intermittently?

indicators.note: intermittently means taking letters at intervals, every other one of bedrooms

explanation.surface: A voyeur peeps into bedrooms now and then to watch what goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of bedrooms gives the god; 'observed peeking into' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of sexual desire is the source from which lovemaking springs.

clue.text: Implement dated renovation of hotel — and what follows?

indicators.note: a renovation remakes something, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet India, I, follows Hotel

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned refit of a hotel, and what comes next?
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovation of' rearranges HOTEL plus I; I comes from India, the code word after Hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An eolith is a crude flint tool from the very early Stone Age, so an ancient implement.

clue.text: Fancy that chap about closing time

indicators.note: closing means the first piece shuts around the second

parts.note: CA (circa) is the abbreviation for about
that chap is him
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Imagine that man hanging about at chucking-out time.
explanation.walkthrough: Closing time suggests a pub in Britain, but 'closing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimaera is a wild fantasy or illusion, a figment of the imagination.

clue.text: Flash Greek's written in centre of Chomsky's scaled chart

indicators.note: written in the centre of means put into the middle of the next word

parts.note: Noam Chomsky is the American linguist
a mo, short for moment, is a flash
GR is an abbreviation for Greek

explanation.surface: A quick Greek note is inked into the middle of a linguist's graded diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomogram is a graph of scaled lines read with a ruler to solve a formula.

clue.text: Too many cuppas might produce this belief

definitions.text: Too many cuppas might produce this
definitions.meaning: a medical term for illness from drinking too much tea, named from theine, the tea alkaloid

explanation.surface: Drinking tea to excess might lead a person to faith.
explanation.walkthrough: A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea; the rarely used medical sense is named from theine, tea's caffeine.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is chronic poisoning from excessive tea; the other is faith in a deity who created the world.

clue.text: Divine ring fits fine

indicators.note: fits means the ring is fitted inside the other word

parts.note: godly means divine or devout
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A heavenly ring fits perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodly is an old word for fine, handsome or considerable.

clue.text: Removal of pants procedure on return from mission?

definitions.meaning: jokily, taking off briefs, which are pants (underpants in Britain)
the questioning of an agent or pilot after an operation

explanation.surface: Taking off one's underwear is the routine after a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants means underpants, so briefs are pants.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally de-briefs, undressing; ordinarily the formal questioning of someone back from an assignment.

clue.text: Planning to dispose of one arrangement

indicators.note: to dispose of means getting rid of one letter

parts.note: an ordinance is something ordained, a planned decree or ordering
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Planning to throw out a single arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses an archaic sense: the word once meant ordering or arrangement, being a variant of ordinance.
explanation.definitionFit: In its old sense, a variant of ordinance, it meant an ordering or disposition of things.

clue.text: Knights I can upset in US comedy show

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece goes inside the show's name

parts.note: Cheers is the American sitcom set in a Boston bar

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom

parts.note: can and lav are both slang for toilet

explanation.surface: Knights take offence at a US sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns I + LAV into VALI, which sits in CHEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevaliers are French knights, or members of an order of chivalry.

clue.text: Main branch line, one mile: Little Britain

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
B, a short form of Britain

explanation.surface: A main railway branch line runs one mile through a little corner of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Britain is also a British TV sketch show, a red herring here.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is one of the large boughs of a tree.

clue.text: Weakness of mind of young mare with love for single

indicators.note: with ... for means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: a filly is a young female horse
I, the Roman numeral one, is single
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lovesick young mare foolishly gives up her single life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with love for single' swaps the I in FILLY for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Folly is foolishness, a lack of good sense.

clue.text: Filling chucked away by Turkish food activist?

indicators.note: the filling of a word is its middle letter, here thrown out

parts.note: a doner kebab is Turkish spit-roasted meat

explanation.surface: Someone throws away the stuffing of a kebab.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter N of DONER, the filling, is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A doer is a person of action, one who acts rather than talks.

clue.text: Not liking manure, losing love of Caribbean island

parts.note: anti means against or not liking

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: guano is bird droppings used as manure
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A gardener who dislikes manure loses their love for a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: An Antiguan is from Antigua in the West Indies, so describes something of that island.

clue.text: Little cultivation

parts.note: growing small things: the Japanese art of growing trees kept tiny

explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the craft of dwarfing trees in pots, horticulture in miniature.

clue.text: Top moulding goes round what?

indicators.note: goes round means the moulding surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a bead is a narrow rounded moulding in carpentry
eh, like what?, asks someone to repeat themselves

explanation.surface: A decorative top moulding goes round... sorry, what?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a noun but is the verb: to top someone is slang for to kill them.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is to kill, and decapitation is one way.

clue.text: A font that's different describes name of healthy food

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around, so the anagram goes round a letter
a font that is different has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A typeface that's unusual is used for the label of a health food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's different' rearranges A FONT, which goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonfat describes food with all the fat removed, eaten as a slimming choice.

clue.text: Sarkozy's holding up ladies' fingers?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom upward
the name Sarkozy holds some letters inside it

explanation.surface: The French president is holding up a woman's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: ARKO, inside Sarkozy, is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady's fingers is another name for the green pod vegetable gumbo.

clue.text: Not evocative of the superhuman active in our niche

indicators.note: active suggests the letters are busy moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Something in our little corner falls short of superhero status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'active' rearranges OUR NICHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unheroic means lacking courage or grandeur, nothing like a hero.

clue.text: Bootless young woman heading north to a Baltic city

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means read upwards
bootless means losing the foot, the final letter, of the word

parts.note: a girl is a young woman

explanation.surface: A barefoot girl travels north to a city on the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: GIRL loses its last letter to give GIR, which heads north as RIG; then add A.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital of Latvia, on the Baltic Sea.

annotationWithheld.clue: Doctor injecting into two pens a cocktail of gin and water from here?

clue.text: In abundance, the force set back VP

indicators.note: set back means one letter is moved further back in the word

parts.note: galore means in abundance
G is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: With plenty of strength, the force pushes back a vice-president.
explanation.walkthrough: VP is a vice-president: Bill Clinton's deputy, US Vice-President 1993-2001.
explanation.definitionFit: He served as US Vice-President under Bill Clinton.

clue.text: Nurse's time to take aim

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse in Britain
D for day, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A nurse's moment to take aim.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is a purpose or goal, as in to that end.
